paragraphs.source_en:
Anashuya [sings]. I have forgiven, 0 new star!
 Maybe you have not heard of us, you have come forth so newly,
You hunter of the fields afar!
 Ah, you will know my loved one by his hunter's arrows truly, 8o
Shoot on him shafts of quietness, that he may ever keep
A lonely laughter, and may kiss his hands to me in sleep.
 Farewell, Vijaya. Nay, no word, no word;
I, priestess of this temple, offer up
Prayers for the land.
 [Vijaya goes.]
0 Brahma, guard in sleep
The merry lambs and the complacent kine,
The Hies below the leaves, and the young mice
In the tree roots, and all the sacred Hocks
Of red flamingoes; and my love, Vijaya;
And may no restless fay with fidget finger go
Trouble his sleeping: give him dreams of me.

paragraphs.source_en:
5 The Indian upon God
I passed along the water's edge below the humid trees,
My spirit rocked in evening light, the rushes round my knees,
My spirit rocked in sleep and sighs; and saw the moorfowl pace
All dripping on a grassy slope, and saw them cease to chase
Each other round in circles, and heard the eldest speak:
Who holds the world between His bill and made us strong or weak
Is an undying moorfowl, and He lives beyond the sky.
 The rains are from His dripping wing, the moonbeams from His eye.
 I passed a little further on and heard a lotus talk:
Who made the world and ruleth it, He hangeth on a stalk, 10
For I am in His image made, and all this tinkling tide
Is but a sliding drop of rain between His petals wide.
 A little way within the gloom a roebuck raised his eyes
Brimful of starlight, and he said: The Stamper of the Skies,
He is a gentle roebuck; for how else, I pray, could He
Conceive a thing so sad and soft, a gentle thing like me?
